core_intuitions: At a fixed parameter budget the body scales as ~12.25 d^2 L, so the product d^2*L is pinned: you buy width or depth with the same currency. At small scale (100M) depth wins because capability is bottlenecked by the number of sequential nonlinear transformations the residual stream can undergo, not the width of each — hence deep-and-thin (512 wide, 30 layers, width-per-layer ~17 vs GPT-2's ~64).

A handful of big tensors dominate a 100M model, so cheap-but-good choices compound: tying embeddings saves ~16.8M (a sixth of the model), a 32k vs 50k vocab frees ~9M (~3 layers), GQA shrinks W_K/W_V 4x — and every freed parameter is spent on more depth. ~17% of params live in the embedding, ~83% in the body, by design.

GQA is the middle of the MHA<->MQA spectrum: 8 query heads share 2 KV heads (4:1 groups), so only 2 heads' worth of K,V are stored/moved instead of 8 — a 4x smaller KV cache (~30 KB/token vs ~120 KB) at near-MHA quality. The KV heads are the memory-expensive part; queries are free.

Attention-logit blowup is the canonical high-LR death: as W_Q,W_K grow, the scaled dot product q.k can exceed ~100, softmax collapses to a hard argmax, gradient to the losing logits ~e^-100 ~ 0, learning freezes and the run NaNs. QK-norm makes it structurally impossible: RMS-normalizing q and k fixes ||q||,||k||~sqrt(d_h)=8, so by Cauchy-Schwarz |q.k|<=64 and after 1/sqrt(d_h) scaling the logit is bounded by ~8 by construction — this is what buys the aggressive Muon learning rate.

Pre-norm keeps a clean identity residual path so 30 layers train without warmup gymnastics; stability is engineered from stacked cheap guards (RMSNorm in fp32, QK-norm, z-loss on the log-partition, optional soft-caps, and 1/sqrt(2L) residual-projection init so accumulated variance stays O(1) not O(L)).

Position is a per-layer choice, not a global one: RoPE rotates q,k so attention depends only on relative offset (23 layers), while every 4th layer uses NoPE — the causal mask alone leaks absolute position, and NoPE layers aren't tied to training-time rotation frequencies, so the mixture extrapolates to longer contexts (the 2048->8192 extension) while RoPE layers keep short-context precision.

new_figures.name: deep-thin-budget-trade
new_figures.concept: A fixed parameter budget spent two ways — shallow-and-wide vs deep-and-thin — showing that d^2*L is pinned so doubling width costs three-quarters of your layers, plus why depth (sequential reasoning steps) wins at small scale.
new_figures.rationale: This is THE governing macro-decision of the whole chapter, made 'before a single line of code', and it currently has no visual. The reader must feel that width and depth are bought with the same currency (d^2*L fixed) and that at 100M the currency buys more capability as depth because depth = sequential nonlinear transformations the residual stream can compose. Making the aspect-ratio trade and the width-per-layer contrast (17 vs 64) visible is the single highest-leverage figure in the chapter.
new_figures.brief: Two side-by-side model schematics that both fill the SAME fixed 'budget' bar (draw a shared budget frame or equal-area callout labelled 'fixed ~84.5M body params, d^2*L pinned'). LEFT, 'shallow-and-wide (GPT-2-small shape)': a short stack of a few very WIDE blocks — e.g. 12 fat blocks, each drawn wide — annotated d_model=768, n_layers=12, width-per-layer d/L ~= 64. RIGHT, 'deep-and-thin (Stack-100M)': a tall stack of many NARROW blocks — e.g. 30 thin blocks — annotated d_model=512, n_layers=30, width-per-layer d/L ~= 17, with a small '~4x thinner per layer' tag. Between them a short equation strip: 'per-layer ~= 12.25 d^2  =>  body ~= 12.25 d^2 L  =>  double d costs 3/4 of your layers'. Along the RIGHT (deep) stack draw a downward flowing arrow through the blocks labelled 'sequential nonlinear transforms = reasoning depth (what small models are bottlenecked on)'; along the LEFT stack a wide sideways arrow labelled 'lots stored per token, few compositional steps'. Bottom takeaway strip: 'at ~100M the evidence flips to depth (MobileLLM 2024); at ~100B width and depth trade evenly.' Use theme-safe CSS vars (an accent for the deep/winning side, a muted tone for the shallow side); only the chapter's own integers (512,768,30,12,17,64) — invent no benchmark numbers. Everything inside the viewBox, clear left-to-right reading order; a single static frame conveys it fully.

new_figures.name: param-budget-allocation

new_figures.rationale: The chapter demands the reader 'reproduce this arithmetic by hand' and the Interview Corner hinges on why each specific number beats the obvious default. A single figure that shows the budget as concrete proportions — a sixth in the lookup table, five-sixths in the body, and inside one block the SwiGLU dwarfing attention — makes the compounding lever story (tie saves ~16.8M, 32k vs 50k frees ~9M ~= 3 layers, GQA cuts W_K/W_V 4x) visible as budget moving into depth. Complements the aspect-ratio figure: that one is WHY depth, this one is WHERE the params physically sit.

new_figures.name: gqa-head-sharing-kv-cache
new_figures.concept: 8 query heads sharing 2 KV heads (4:1 groups) as the middle of the MHA<->MQA spectrum, with the concrete consequence: the KV cache stores only 2 heads' worth of K,V — 4x smaller than MHA (~30 KB/token vs ~120 KB).
new_figures.rationale: GQA is the chapter's single most consequential attention choice and drives both a param saving and the serving-critical 4x KV-cache win that the worked example and Interview Corner return to. A picture of 8 query heads fanning into 2 shared KV heads, paired with the two cache footprints drawn to scale, makes 'the KV heads are the expensive part, queries are free' click far faster than the repeat_interleave code. Foundational for the memory intuition the serving chapters build on.
new_figures.brief: Top panel — head routing: draw 8 query-head boxes in a row (Q0..Q7) and 2 KV-head boxes (KV0, KV1) below. Group Q0..Q3 with connectors down to KV0 and Q4..Q7 to KV1, labelling the fan-in 'groups = 8/2 = 4 query heads per KV head'. Show a small spectrum ribbon above it positioning this design: 'MHA (8 KV, max quality/max cache) ---- [GQA 2 KV, here] ---- MQA (1 KV, min cache)'. Note beside the KV boxes: 'K,V computed narrow (512->128) then shared; a real kernel never materializes the expansion — it reads the shared KV head directly'. Bottom panel — KV cache footprint, drawn to scale: two horizontal memory bars for one token across 30 layers, bf16. 'GQA (2 KV heads): 2(K,V) x 2 x 64 x 30 x 2 bytes = ~30 KB/token' as a short bar; 'MHA (8 KV heads): ~120 KB/token' as a bar 4x longer, with a bracket '4x'. Add a single caption 'full 2048-context: ~60 MB (GQA) vs ~240 MB (MHA) — the win that makes it cheap to serve'. Use theme-safe CSS vars (accent for the two KV heads / GQA bar, muted for the query heads and the MHA bar); integers are the chapter's own (8,2,4,64,30,30 KB,120 KB,60 MB,240 MB,512,128) — invent none. Everything inside the viewBox; the two cache bars MUST be length-accurate (4:1) so the saving is literal, not decorative. Static frame suffices.

new_figures.name: qk-norm-logit-bound
new_figures.concept: The attention-logit blowup failure mode vs the QK-norm fix, side by side: without QK-norm the scaled q.k grows unbounded until softmax becomes a hard argmax and the gradient to losing logits vanishes (run NaNs); with QK-norm ||q||,||k|| are fixed so Cauchy-Schwarz caps the logit at ~8 by construction.
new_figures.rationale: Stability is a headline theme of the chapter ('engineered, not hoped for') and QK-norm is explicitly 'what buys the high learning rate that makes the run cheap'. The worked example is a quantitative causal chain that a two-regime figure makes visceral: readers should SEE the runaway logit -> saturated softmax -> frozen gradient death, and the structural bound that removes it. This is the deepest mechanistic 'why' in the residual-stream section and has no visual.
new_figures.brief: Two vertical lanes sharing the header 'pre-softmax logit = (q.k)/sqrt(d_h), d_h=64'. LEFT lane 'WITHOUT QK-norm (blows up)': step 1 'W_Q,W_K drift up -> per-component std sigma grows (say sigma->6)'; step 2 'q.k std ~= sigma^2 sqrt(d_h) = 8 sigma^2, after /8 scaling ~= sigma^2 -> ~36; max over 2048 tokens can exceed 100' with a small logit-bar chart showing one towering bar dwarfing the rest; step 3 a softmax distribution drawn as a near one-hot spike labelled 'hard argmax'; step 4 a danger badge 'grad to losing logits ~ e^-100 ~ 0 -> attention frozen -> loss NaN'. Mark this lane broken (struck arrow / break glyph). RIGHT lane 'WITH QK-norm (bounded by construction)': step 1 'RMSNorm q,k over head_dim -> ||q||,||k|| ~= sqrt(d_h) = 8 regardless of projection growth'; step 2 'Cauchy-Schwarz: |q.k| <= ||q|| ||k|| = 64, after /8 scaling logit bounded by +-8' with a small logit-bar chart whose bars are comparable in height (a soft distribution); step 3 a softmax drawn as a smooth spread-out distribution labelled 'stays soft -> gradient flows'; step 4 a good badge 'blow-up structurally impossible; learned temperature via RMSNorm gamma'. Between the lanes a one-line contrast 'removes the failure mode, not tiptoes around it (why QK-norm > merely a lower LR)'. Use theme-safe CSS vars (danger accent for the blow-up lane's spike/NaN, good accent for the bounded lane); all numbers (64,8,sigma=6,36,100,e^-100) are from the chapter's worked example — invent none. Both little softmax pictures must read at a glance (one spike vs one spread). Static frame conveys the whole causal chain; no animation needed.

new_figures.name: rope-nope-layer-stack
new_figures.concept: The 30-layer stack colored by positional scheme — 23 RoPE layers (local relative-position precision) interleaved with 7 NoPE layers (every 4th, for length extrapolation) — and why the causal mask lets NoPE layers still infer position.
new_figures.rationale: NoPE-every-4th-layer is flagged as 'a genuinely modern choice' unique to this chapter (SmolLM3, 2025) and is the stated ingredient behind the 2048->8192 context extension. The pattern (which layers, why the mixture rather than pure RoPE) is inherently spatial across the depth axis and reads instantly as a colored column, versus the modular-arithmetic prose '(l+1) mod 4 == 0'. A small, high-clarity figure that pins down both the WHICH and the WHY of the hybrid.
new_figures.brief: A vertical column of 30 stacked layer cells indexed 0..29 (bottom to top or top to bottom, pick one and label direction). Color 23 of them as 'RoPE' (accent A) and the 7 every-4th layers — indices 3,7,11,15,19,23,27, i.e. (l+1) mod 4 == 0 — as 'NoPE' (accent B), clearly interleaved 3-then-1. A legend: 'RoPE x23: rotate q,k -> attention depends on relative offset (local precision, sample-efficient short context)'; 'NoPE x7 (every 4th): no injected position'. Beside a NoPE cell, a small callout explaining the why: 'causal mask already leaks absolute position (a token sees only its predecessors -> its count is a position signal); NoPE layers aren't tied to training rotation frequencies -> extrapolate to longer sequences'. A bottom band ties it to context extension: 'RoPE for local precision + NoPE for length robustness -> the mixture behind 2048 -> 8192 in mid-training; the 1-in-4 ratio is SmolLM3's tuned constant, not a law'. Add a small warning aside 'pure NoPE underperforms on SHORT context — that's why we interleave, not remove'. Use theme-safe CSS vars for the two accents; integers are the chapter's own (30,23,7,4, indices 3..27). Everything inside the viewBox, one clear reading order; static frame suffices.

summary: A concept-dense capstone chapter with ZERO figures — the highest-leverage opportunity is to give its foundational bets pictures. The full block/model data flow is already served well by the chapter's own ASCII diagram, so I do NOT propose a redundant architecture figure; instead I target the five intuitions that carry the chapter and have no visual. Priority-1 must-haves: (1) deep-thin-budget-trade — the governing macro-decision, d^2*L pinned so width and depth are bought with one currency, and why depth wins at 100M; (2) param-budget-allocation — where ~101.3M physically sits (17% tied embedding, 83% body; SwiGLU dwarfs attention per block) and how the tie/32k-vocab/GQA levers move budget into layers, so the reader can reproduce the arithmetic; (3) gqa-head-sharing-kv-cache — 8 query heads into 2 KV heads and the length-accurate 4x KV-cache saving that the serving chapters lean on; (4) qk-norm-logit-bound — the logit-blowup death vs the Cauchy-Schwarz bound QK-norm imposes, the chapter's deepest stability mechanism and what buys the high Muon LR. Priority-2: (5) rope-nope-layer-stack — the 23-RoPE/7-NoPE interleave (SmolLM3) behind the 2048->8192 extension, a spatial pattern that reads far better as a colored depth column than as prose. All five are single-frame insights; none need animation. Every brief stays theme-safe and uses only the chapter's own integers.
